research_constraints.summary: Outcome shape Success(value, receipt) | Failed(typed, receipt) | Refused(reason) | Indeterminate(recovery id); Indeterminate maps to DELIVERY_UNKNOWN (owner outcomes COMMITTED / REFUSED / DELIVERY_UNKNOWN).
Crash, unavailable authority, or a missing / stale / mismatched record is UNKNOWN: never REFUSED and never success.
No retry without an idempotency proof.
Consumed authority and current validity are separate fields (one enum cannot carry both).

Claim and revoke compete on ONE authoritative per-capability state: OPEN -> CLAIMED | REVOKED; CLAIMED -> COMMITTED | FAILED | INDETERMINATE; every unlisted transition refuses. Release at the result sink is the commit point.

Release requires all three: independent authorization; prepared-result custody; operation- and generation-bound evidence that every required pre-release cleanup succeeded. Cleanup evidence NotRequired only when the obligation set is provably empty; Pending / Failed / Unknown refuse.
No ordinary result extraction before that release guard.
Free is not wipe.
Refusal after reservation/consumption never restores authority.
FFI / host aliases are not contained by ownership alone (OPEN).

open_items: Ordering of actual release vs effective revocation (including partial sends).

astra_outcome_wording.W1: In the current profile COMMITTED is unreachable after begin (B) for every out-of-process release. This is a policy restriction, not a theorem. A signed recipient receipt is observation only and cannot change the current outcome.
astra_outcome_wording.W2: Ordinary write or send completion does not establish durable recipient effect. fsync is stronger than plain write acceptance, but neither local persistence nor a successful close establishes recipient effect. None of this moves release from B to a later flush or changes post-B DELIVERY_UNKNOWN.
astra_outcome_wording.W3: DELIVERY_UNKNOWN and any UNKNOWN is never success, never proof of zero effect, and never authority to retry or re-admit. Recovery runs before new claims and never promotes or reissues. Missing, stale or corrupt evidence stays UNKNOWN and closes admission.
astra_outcome_wording.W4: Choose the profile from demonstrated exposure and custody topology, never from API names. B precedes the earliest usable exposure, including a capability handoff or a store into already shared memory. Unclear topology refuses before B; a missing profile never selects the in-process success table.
astra_outcome_wording.W5: After DELIVERY_UNKNOWN an unproved retry can duplicate an effect, so automatic retry is prohibited. Keep effect retry and disclosure retry separate.
astra_outcome_wording.committed_after_B_out_of_process: unreachable by policy, not as a theorem

memory_blockers.rule: A re-issue gets its own typed code, distinct from a fresh mint; an unlisted lease state refuses with 111; a forged issued id refuses.
Range-check every token first (unlisted -> 111), then decide.
Refuse release unless independent authorization, prepared-result custody, and cleanup evidence bound to operation and generation are all present and valid.

Cleanup evidence is a sealed value the cleanup module mints; the guard admits only DONE with matching opId, generation and digest, or NOT_REQUIRED for a statically empty obligation set; anything else refuses before begin; failed or unknown cleanup after begin is QUARANTINED with DELIVERY_UNKNOWN.
Every adapter declares an observation class; an unaudited pre-begin path is OUT_OF_PROCESS_UNBOUND and release counts at its first buffered write.

The v1 memory profile is single process with in-memory cells; restart starts a new incarnation epoch; any earlier-incarnation op id recovers as DELIVERY_UNKNOWN and is never retried; a multi-process or durable deployment refuses CROSS_PROCESS_CAS_NOT_VERIFIABLE.
A startup recovery pass marks every non-terminal cell ABANDONED (DELIVERY_UNKNOWN) before any claim is admitted, plus the MB-08 incarnation rule.
COMMITTED is unreachable for out-of-process classes; an ack is recorded as evidence only and never upgrades DELIVERY_UNKNOWN.

v1 admits only host-import release into non-shared WebAssembly.Memory as IN_PROCESS_BOUND; SharedArrayBuffer, shared WebAssembly.Memory, MessagePort copy/transfer, mmap, fd passing and resizable buffers refuse ADAPTER_CLASS_NOT_ADMITTED; no erase claim.
